Plane | Project management tool for issues, sprints and roadmaps

summary.one_liner: Plane is an open-source, self-hostable project management tool for tracking issues, cycles (sprints), modules, and product roadmaps, offered as a cloud service or self-hosted via Docker or Kubernetes.
summary.what_it_does: Plane is a project management application for tracking issues (called work items), running cycles (sprints) with burn-down charts, and dividing larger efforts into modules. Work items support a rich text editor with file uploads, sub-properties, and references to related issues. Users can create filters as views, save them, and share them with others. Pages let users capture notes with a rich text editor and AI capabilities, and convert notes into actionable items. An analytics section is described as providing real-time insights across project data. The README offers a hosted Plane Cloud option as well as self-hosting, with Docker and Kubernetes listed as installation methods, and instance admins can configure settings via "God mode".
use_cases: track software development issues and bugs
split a large project into modules
capture meeting or project notes and turn them into tasks
how_to_run: Sign up for a free account on Plane Cloud (hosted option)
For self-hosting, follow the Plane deployment guides linked in the README (Docker or Kubernetes)
notable: Offered both as a hosted Plane Cloud service and as a self-hosted install
Cycles with burn-down charts for sprint-style tracking
Pages with a rich text editor and AI capabilities
Listed as an alternative to JIRA, Linear and Height in awesome-selfhosted
caveats: Self-hosting requires setting up your own servers via the linked deployment guides; the README does not detail requirements
README states the project is evolving daily, so features may change
Some features are described as AI-assisted; the README does not detail how these work
